title: Corey Haines's Sales Enablement skill: collateral reps actually use and can defend
summary: An AI-agent playbook for building B2B sales collateral (decks, one-pagers, objection docs, battle cards, demo scripts, win-loss analysis). The core idea is that sales uses what sales trusts: situation-specific, scannable, outcome-tied, and built from claims reps can defend in front of buyers.

principles.text: Involve reps in creating collateral and use their language, or they will rewrite it.
principles.quote: Involve reps in creation. Use their language, not marketing's. If reps rewrite your deck before sending it, you wrote the wrong deck. Test drafts with your top performers first.

principles.text: Tailor collateral to persona, deal stage and use case rather than going generic.
principles.quote: Tailor to persona, deal stage, and use case. A deck for a CTO should look different from one for a VP of Sales.

principles.text: Make sales docs scannable: reps need the answer in seconds mid-call.
principles.quote: Reps need information in 3 seconds, not 30. Use bold headers, short bullets, and visual hierarchy. If a rep can't find the answer mid-call, the doc has failed.

principles.text: Tie every claim to a business outcome, not a feature label.
principles.quote: Every claim connects to revenue, efficiency, or risk reduction. Features mean nothing without the "so what." Replace "AI-powered analytics" with "cut reporting time by 80%."

principles.text: Only write claims buyers can't disprove; back 'why we win' with evidence and admit where you lose.
principles.quote: Reps repeat what you write to buyers who can check it. Anything a buyer can disprove in a minute costs more than it gains.

principles.text: Run demos after discovery, customized to the buyer's use case, with the prospect talking.
principles.quote: Demo after discovery, not before. If you don't know their pain, you're guessing which features matter.
